newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers begin work on traffic pollution curbs.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers begin work on traffic pollution curbs.

text.p: European Union environment ministers began on Thursday what could be a drawn-out session in search of a deal to cut pollution from road traffic by setting tougher engine emission and fuel quality standards for cars.
"It will probably drag out quite a while," a European Commission official told reporters at the start of talks.

Ministers are to tackle two European Commission proposals drawn up after its joint Auto/Oil research programme with the oil and car industries and launched last year amid some controversy about the targets set and methods used.
The first proposal is to set emission norms for new diesel and petrol-engined cars from the year 2000 while the second deals with quality norms for petrol and diesel fuels.

Ministers are divided on a variety of points, in particular on allowed levels of benzene and sulphur in petrol and sulphur in diesel as well the question of whether to set strict 2005 targets for engines and fuels now or to wait and watch progress.
The Dutch, as EU presidency holders, are intent on a deal to cap their six-month term at the helm which ends this month.
"On Auto/Oil, the presidency is determined to find a solution," the official said.

Other agenda items set for detailed talks on Thursday and Friday include plans to cut emissions of volatile solvents used by industry and the EU's position on reducing emissions of climate change gases such as carbon dioxide from fossil fuels.
